after: The Wrinkles are watching every door out of that castle. If they move her again, we will know.

speaker: Wren
before: Her name goes in the true record, whatever else happens.
after: Her name goes into the true record, whatever else happens. I can promise you that much.

speaker: Primm
before: Ah, a visitor. Do come in; I so rarely receive anyone who has not been summoned.
after: Ah, a visitor. Do come in. I so rarely receive anyone who has not been summoned.

speaker: Primm
before: You have walked the whole length of my castle. You have, I notice, scuffed it.
after: You have walked the whole length of my castle to reach this room. You have also, I notice, scuffed it.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: Sorry, that's forest mud. I've walked a long way to get here, and everyone I met on the road was afraid of you.
after: I'm sorry about the floor. It's forest mud. I've walked a long way to get here, and everyone I met on the road was afraid of you.

speaker: Primm
before: Afraid? Of order, perhaps, or of comfort, or of the dreadful burden of being safe?
after: Afraid? Of order, perhaps? Of comfort? Of the dreadful burden of being kept safe?

speaker: Primm
before: I have given them roofs, and hats, and rules, and I have given each of them exactly the same amount of each, which is more than anyone before me ever managed.
after: I have given them roofs, and hats, and rules, and I have given every one of them exactly the same amount of each, which is more than anyone before me ever managed.

speaker: Primm
before: Ten years I have been mending this kingdom. Ten years, and still you come, with your different hats and your different opinions, to undo the only good thing anyone has ever done.
after: For ten years I have been mending this kingdom. Ten years, and still you people come, with your different hats and your different opinions, to undo the only good thing anyone has ever done for it.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: Because some things are five. Some people are.
after: Because some things are five. Some people are, too.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: I met a man who'd been locked up for ten years without a single weight, and he could still lift me off the floor. Strength is what you do with what's left, and strength is not control.
after: I met a man who was locked up for ten years without a single weight, and he could still lift me off the floor. Strength is what you do with whatever is left to you, and strength is not control.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: Because some things are five. Some people are.
after: Because some things are five. Some people are, too.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: You copied my cards, but what I do with them is mine. I watched a cook give her own name away and stay exactly herself, so I know a name's a blank page until you sign it.
after: You copied my cards, but what I do with them is mine. I watched a cook give her own name away and stay exactly who she was, so I know a name is a blank page until you sign it.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: I spent ten years filed under 'subject'. Never again, not me and not anyone else. No order you could write outranks treating people with respect.
after: And I spent ten years filed under 'subject'. Never again, for me or for anyone. No order you could ever write outranks treating people with respect.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: You copied my cards, but what I do with them is mine. I watched a cook give her own name away and stay exactly herself, so I know a name's a blank page until you sign it.
after: You copied my cards, but what I do with them is mine. I watched a cook give her own name away and stay exactly who she was, so I know a name is a blank page until you sign it.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: I spent ten years filed under 'subject'. Never again, not me and not anyone else. No order you could write outranks treating people with respect.
after: I spent ten years filed under 'subject'. Never again, for me or for anyone. No order you could ever write outranks treating people with respect.

speaker: Primm
before: I made... (he stops.) I made them, and they were good. Then I put my name on every one, and I stopped asking anyone whether they wanted the next.
after: I made... (he stops.) I made them, and they were good. And then I put my name on every one, and I stopped asking anyone whether they wanted the next.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: I'm not going to correct you; that was always your way. I'm not going to forgive you either, not today. Start smaller than a kingdom. Say sorry to one person.
after: I'm not going to correct you. That was always your way of doing things. And I'm not going to forgive you either, not today. Start with something smaller than a kingdom. Say sorry to one person.

speaker: Primm
before: One? I corrected eleven thousand. Where would I even begin? I cannot remember a single one of their names.
after: One? I corrected eleven thousand of them. Where would I even begin? I cannot remember a single one of their names.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: '{prince},' she says, loud enough for the whole plaza to hear. She has said it in her kitchen; this is the first time she has said it to the kingdom. 'Welcome home.'
after: '{prince},' she says, loudly enough for the whole plaza to hear. She has said it in her kitchen, but this is the first time she has said it to the kingdom. 'Welcome home.'

speaker: (narration)
before: A game about a kingdom that was strong because it was not the same.
after: A game about a kingdom that was strong because its pieces did not match.

speaker: (check key)
before: The kingdom is whole again, and it is yours to walk.
after: The kingdom is in one piece again, seams and all, and it is yours to walk.

speaker: Wren
before: You did it. Sit down a moment. I'm Wren, Royal Archivist, and for ten years I kept the only honest record in this city.
after: You did it. Sit down for a moment. I'm Wren, the Royal Archivist, and for ten years I kept the only honest record in this city.

speaker: Wren
before: The Crease is just a cellar now, but we're keeping it. Too many true things were written down there to let it go.
after: The Crease is only a cellar now, but we are keeping it. Too many true things were written down here to let it go.

speaker: Wren
before: The kingdom is mending one argument at a time, and it's dreadfully inefficient. I've never been happier. Take your time.
after: The kingdom is mending itself one argument at a time, and it's dreadfully inefficient. I have never been happier. Take your time.
